chunks: And whatever was scattered in it regarding the legal cases of Amir Al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Jafar, peace be upon him.

key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in Shia hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of narration for the legal cases of Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage functions as a scholarly colophon in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, validating the authenticity of scattered legal precedents (qadaya) attributed to Imam Ali by tracing them through a reliable chain to Imam al-Baqir. It highlights the methodological rigor of Shaykh al-Saduq in preserving the jurisprudential legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring that these rulings are recognized as part of the Imami legal tradition rather than isolated historical anecdotes.
